output.name: Hessak

anatomy.part: the grip, the rounded knob at the top-right end of the bone shaft
the shank bend, where the long shaft turns steeply down into the hook
the belly of the hook, the lowest point of its bowl
the left arm of the hook, midway up its curve toward the barb
the barb tip, curling back toward the shaft

output.myth: Kessa went out on the sea-ice one grey morning, when the wind had dropped and the ice was singing. A man had gone through near the shelves. His coat had spread out under the water like a sail. Kessa had only her bone hook and a length of gut. She lay flat and felt about with the hook until it caught in his collar. Then she pulled. He came up grey as a gutted fish and did not breathe for a long time. Then he did. Tavo laughed when he heard, as he laughs at everything he has not wrecked yet. Kael, who has cast for fallen stars since before the islands had names, said nothing. Kessa hung the hook on the sky to dry, and it is there still. Look south when the ice is moving. The hook catches the cold light and will not let it go. Some nights the drowned man's coat hangs from it, waiting to be flown.
output.verse:
Grey ice, a bone hook
catches the cold southern light
it will not let go
